description: CALL THIS BEFORE YOUR AGENT SIGNS ANYTHING THAT MOVES MONEY. One request instead of five: it reads the counterparty record, decodes the calldata you are about to sign, looks up the seller’s own catalogue listing, runs an unpaid 402 handshake with the endpoint, and applies a published policy — and then, which is the point, compares them WITH EACH OTHER. The losses an agent actually suffers live between those readings and no single one of them can see them: the bytes paying an address you never checked, so a spotless counterparty record is about a party this transaction does not pay; an UNLIMITED APPROVAL wearing the shape of a one-cent payment; the seller’s listing naming a payee the calldata does not; a policy allowing a payment for a path that is not served. Every cross-check names BOTH readings that disagree in `between`, and none of them is an accusation — the record can be wrong. Send `calldata` whenever you have it: it unlocks the strongest check there is. A cross-check can only make the verdict worse, never better. Nothing is simulated: the transaction is read, never executed. `ran` says which parts did not run and why, because a check that did not happen must never look like one that passed. PAID; its five components are each free on their own tools and what is sold here is the comparison.

amountUsd.description: What is about to be sent, in dollars.

calldata.description: The hex bytes you are about to sign. Left out, the transaction is reported as UNREAD rather than fine.

chain.description: The chain it is about to be sent on, e.g. base.

policy.description: A policy slug or version from list_policies. Defaults to conservative.

recipient.description: The address about to be paid.

resource.description: The http(s) URL of the endpoint being bought, where there is one.

name: check_action

crossChecks.description: The comparisons between parts. Each names the TWO readings that disagree. The ones that AGREED are published too, because a comparison that ran and agreed is different from one that never ran.

limits.description: What this check structurally cannot contain: what the action is FOR, terms agreed privately, any simulation, and calls the decoder refuses rather than guesses at. Read it before treating a clean answer as a safe one.

parts.description: Each reading on its own: policy, transaction, listing, endpoint, settledOn.

ran.description: Which parts ran and why each one did not.

says.description: The worst thing found, in one sentence.

verdict.description: The policy’s decision, worsened by the cross-checks and never improved by them.

title: One check before you sign (paid)
